subject: SIG submission: on-prem peering proof and ephemeral IP allowlist for Helix Therapeutics
messages:
From: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@helixtx.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@helixtx.com
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: network evidence request for peering/private endpoints

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The InfoSec team at Helix needs the SIG network evidence to complete our vendor review. We have a short checklist: VPC peering confirmation or PrivateLink alternative, a network topology diagram showing private endpoints, and any sample peering session logs for the past 30 days.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will provide:
- a short handoff packet for our cloud/network team (diagram + connection steps)
- example TCP/IP allowlist ranges (static or ephemeral ranges you can commit to)
- redacted peering session logs or a sanitized export we can use for audit

We'd like to get this packaged by next Monday (2027-02-22) if possible. Attaching the Helix vendor intake form for reference (Helix fields highlighted).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Sam Hayes
Security Program Manager
Helix Therapeutics
sam.hayes@helixtx.com
+1 415-555-0198
Attachment: helix_vendor_intake_form.pdf (attachment stub)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@helixtx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence request for peering/private endpoints

Sam —

We're on it. High level answers up front: Redwood supports both VPC peering and PrivateLink-style private endpoints depending on customer preference. We can provide a handoff packet with topology, a sample allowlist, and sanitized peering logs. Karthik will assemble the technical artifacts; Monica will coordinate the package and delivery timeline.

Couple quick clarifying items before we package:
- Which cloud provider/region will Helix use for this integration (e.g., us-west-2 vs us-east-1)?
- Do you require a fixed public IP block for outbound egress, or are ephemeral NAT ranges acceptable if we publish an allowlist window?
- Any required retention window for logs (30/90/365 days)?

We plan to deliver an initial zipped packet and a short handoff doc by EOD Mon 2027-02-22 if those answers don't change scope. Attaching the Redwood VPC peering template and a placeholder topology PDF to speed review.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations (acting on security coordination)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_vpc_peering_template.yaml (attachment stub)
Attachment: network-diagram-helix.pdf (attachment stub)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@helixtx.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence request for peering/private endpoints

Sam / team —

Adding the technical details requested. Per our internal routing options:
- Option A (VPC peering): peer the Helix VPC to the Redwood dedicated network for the tenant. Peering is regional (us-west-2) and supports direct private IP reachability. No transit gateway required for single-region peering.
- Option B (PrivateEndpoint/PrivateLink): create a PrivateLink endpoint in your VPC that maps to our private service endpoint. This provides better isolation and avoids route table changes on your side.

Attached artifacts (sanitized):
- peering-session-logs-2027-02-19.csv — sample BGP session up/down records with timestamps (redacted ASNs and public IPs).
- peering-manifest-helix.zip — includes instructions, terraform snippet, and sanitized tcpdump excerpts demonstrating TCP handshake sequence for a test flow.
- network-diagram-helix.pdf (updated) — shows recommended subnets, SGs, and which ports are required (443 TCP for gRPC/HTTPS; 10250 TCP for health checks if enabled).

Regarding the allowlist: Redwood can publish a weekly ephemeral egress range that we update in the console and expose via a signed URL. If Helix requires a static IP block we can provision an egress NAT IP pool for the Dedicated deployment; that requires a short procurement step.

Log retention: we can export 90 days of sanitized peering metrics by default; 365-day retention can be provided as an add-on.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm region (please reply with us-west-2 or us-east-1).
2) Choose Option A or B.
3) If static IPs are required, confirm and we'll include the NAT pool proposal.

Thanks — attaching the technical artifacts now. Let me know if you want a short walkthrough.

—Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: peering-session-logs-2027-02-19.csv (attachment stub); peering-manifest-helix.zip (attachment stub); network-diagram-helix.pdf (attachment stub)
From: Sam Hayes <sam.hayes@helixtx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@helixtx.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence request for peering/private endpoints

Karthik / Lauren —

This is exactly what we needed, thank you. Quick answers:
- Region: us-west-2.
- We'll start with Option B (PrivateLink) for isolation.
- Ephemeral egress ranges are acceptable for now — we'll review static NAT in the production rollout.
- Retention: please include 90 days of sanitized logs for the SIG package.

Request: can you add a simple CSV of the current ephemeral ranges (start/end + effective timestamp) and a one-page checklist we can drop into our Change Management ticket? If you can push those to the Drive link you listed (or to our security_ops mailbox), we can close the Helix SIG task this week. I've attached a short acknowledgement form from our side.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to escalate to a call if any step is blocked.

Sam Hayes
Security Program Manager
Helix Therapeutics
Attachment: helix_request_ack.pdf (attachment stub)
